ideas.title: After Hours (working title): Roblox horror pilots
ideas.logline: Standalone suspense stories with Max, Mia and Leo: an unlisted player copies them across an empty server, a duplicate-player encounter and a night shift.
ideas.notes: Working name, entity and pilot premises are not approved scripts; no videos produced. First pass of the asset kit built and reviewed 2026-10-02 (see the build status in the asset plan).

ideas.title: The Free Coin Trap
ideas.logline: Max finds a free-coin button, holds it down, and gets buried until Mia pays one coin to stop it.
ideas.notes: On TikTok since 2026-09-17 (seen in TikTok Studio 2026-10-05).

ideas.title: The AFK Champion
ideas.logline: Leo is AFK for five rounds of a disaster-survival game and keeps surviving by accident until Max and Mia try to get him kicked.

ideas.title: Admin For One Round
ideas.logline: Leo gets admin commands for one round, spams a useless 'explode' command, and finds out too late that it was aimed at himself.
ideas.platform: TikTok (>60 s for Creator Rewards) / YouTube Shorts
ideas.notes: On TikTok since 2026-09-30 22:35 (seen in TikTok Studio 2026-10-05).

ideas.title: The AFK Millionaire
ideas.logline: Last one in the circle wins a million coins: Leo, Max and Mia take each other out with tricks while the noob never moves, because he was eating dinner.
ideas.platform: TikTok (>60 s for Creator Rewards) / YouTube Shorts

ideas.title: Max Got Admin For One Round
ideas.logline: Max gets admin and spends the round trying to get rid of Leo; every command backfires, the ban lands one second too late, and next round Leo gets admin again.

ideas.title: ViralRoblox News (daily series)
ideas.logline: Daily 65-75 s Roblox news Short with one recurring girl news presenter, a fixed branded news booth, a fixed cover layout and a 'Follow ViralRobloxGames' call to action every episode.
ideas.platform: TikTok (>60 s for Creator Rewards) / YouTube Shorts

ideas.title: Leo Gave Everyone Admin
ideas.logline: Leo means to kick everyone but types admin all; an admin war breaks out (explode, invisible-with-floating-hair, giant, rocket) while Mia quietly types one long command that strips the boys of admin and makes them dance - but she forgot the AFK noob, who still has admin and just got back from dinner.

ideas.title: The Noob Has Admin
ideas.logline: The noob gets admin and turns out to be a pro who counters everyone's signature moves; Mia never moves all round, Leo pokes her and she falls like a plank, then the noob types gg and it posts under Mia's name - the noob is Mia's alt, so in Part 3 she didn't forget him.

ideas.title: Mia Had Two Crowns
ideas.logline: Leo and Max team up against Mia's two accounts, discover only one can move at a time and overwhelm her; she freezes herself on the wrong window, then typos 'admin Leo and Max' - their alliance lasts one second and they kick each other. Mia wins by accident; Skye joins the game.

ideas.title: Every Jump Makes You Bigger
ideas.series: every x makes you y (posted as a standalone)
ideas.logline: In an obby where every jump makes you bigger, Leo jumps fifty times and strides to the finish, which is a tiny door. He blocks it out of spite; Max baits him into jumping to a hundred, the floor breaks and Leo falls out of the map - and respawns at his last checkpoint, right next to the door, tiny again. Leo wins, then does a victory jump in a very small room.

ideas.title: Every Step Makes You Faster
ideas.logline: In a game where every step makes you faster, Leo runs laps of the lobby to speed 1,000, crosses the map in one second and can't stop - off the end of the map three times. Max hops the course (jumps aren't steps) at speed 16. Leo runs circles around Max to blow him into the lava; the wind becomes a tornado that throws Max onto the finish. Leo still can't stop, hits 9,999 and the anti-cheat kicks him for speed hacking. In a speed game.

ideas.title: Stealing a T-Rex Egg
ideas.logline: A Steal an Egg parody on the game's own T-rex and eggs: Leo and Max get flung four ways trying to steal the best egg (headbutt, higher, eaten bush, own bear trap), team up (Max decoys, Leo waddles the giant egg to the safe zone) and hatch a $1/s baby - while Mia, sneaking in the background all video, took the other twelve. They hatch and cry; safe zones stop guardians, not moms: Mom walks in, takes her babies and Mia. Last shot = first shot, with Mia as the egg.

ideas.title: The Super Nose Detective
ideas.logline: A Roblox take on the 70s Miami detective parody Dick Snifford (flirting yes, no swearing or sexual references): Detective Max Sniffwell has the Super Nose gamepass and solves the stolen Golden Donut case by sniffing a sock. Skye asks if he's single and Mia asks him to stay at a pool party ('Tempting. But I'm on a case.'); he sneezes a pepper-throwing red herring into the pool and follows the trail back to Chief Leo, who has one sock, sprinkles on his face and half the donut. Leo slides him the other half, his cut. 'Tempting.' Case closed.
ideas.notes: Posted by the user on TikTok 2026-10-04 16:30 (seen in TikTok Studio 2026-10-05).

ideas.title: The Server Says One
ideas.logline: The server says one player online, but a faceless player stands in front of Max, copying him half a second late. It is his mirror image, and it creeps closer with every copy. Max fakes left, cuts right and slams the EXIT door; the copy, running the wrong way, hits the other side. Then the list updates: two players online. Max. And Max.

ideas.title: Which Max Is Real
ideas.logline: Finale. Mia, who was spectating, realises the copy is a mirror: 'raise your right hand' exposes the right Max (the hoodie star was the clue). It lunges for her; Max walks backwards so the mirror backs toward the EXIT door, it resists one step away, Max sprints backwards and the mirror is flung through; Mia slams the door. Two players online. Max waves goodbye at the door; nothing waves back.
ideas.notes: Posted by the user on TikTok 2026-10-04 23:37 (seen in TikTok Studio 2026-10-05).

ideas.title: Three Seconds
ideas.logline: Leo can stop time, but only for three seconds, which is never enough. When a piano falls toward Mia and she's twenty steps away, he uses his three seconds to throw the dodgeball that once hit him and knocks her clear. Mia asks if he just stopped time. 'Three seconds is cute. I get four.' She freezes him and eats his fries, which is where they kept going.
ideas.notes: Dropped 2026-10-03: the 'I get four' twist was a last-second new rule and the downside was only 'too short'. Replaced by Forty Floors.

ideas.title: Forty Floors
ideas.logline: You're falling forty floors, and you can swap places with anything alive you can see. Swapping saves you but drops the window cleaner in your place, so you swap back. Everyone in sight would fall instead of you, until you see a pigeon. It takes your fall and opens its wings; the window cleaner you spared lowers his platform and pulls you in.

ideas.title: Which Max Rejoined?
ideas.series: After Hours horror (part 2 of 2, finale v3)
ideas.logline: Two Maxes; the mirror test shows the real one is LEFT. The copy isn't late any more and keeps closing in, so Max makes it copy him leaving the game: both disconnect. Max clicks Rejoin and spawns alone, one player online... then sees the star on his hoodie is on the wrong side. The copy rejoined.

ideas.title: The Last Penalty
ideas.logline: You're the keeper facing the last penalty of the final. Leo always looks at the corner he's aiming for, so you dive early and save it, but it's retaken because you left your line. Knowing he's been read, Leo shuts his eyes, and you stay on your line. Unable to see, he scuffs it into the grass and it rolls to your boot.
ideas.notes: Posted by the user on TikTok 2026-10-04 22:01 (seen in TikTok Studio 2026-10-05).

ideas.title: Don't Sneeze Outside
ideas.logline: Every time you sneeze, your gravity flips. Indoors you land on the ceiling; outdoors there's no ceiling. Leo blows a dandelion in Max's face and he falls up, catching a lamppost upside down; only another sneeze brings him down. Leo's pepper falls back on Leo. Mia's cat climbs the pole to his nose: he sneezes and drops to the sidewalk, safe, and the cat jumps on his chest. Ah... ah...
ideas.notes: Dropped 2026-10-04: the user found it boring. Replaced by Every Lie Comes True.

ideas.title: Every Lie Comes True
ideas.logline: Whatever Leo lies about comes true: a dragon eats his homework, he's the fastest kid in school, he has a million dollars. Then he crashes Max's bike and panics: 'I've never seen you before.' Max forgets him. Lying 'you're my best friend' brings Max back, but Max asks who broke the bike; Leo nearly blames the dragon (something lands on the roof) and tells the truth. 'Then you're buying me a new one.' 'Fine. I've got a million dollars.' Two true things in one day.
ideas.notes: Approved 2026-10-05. Scheduled for 2026-10-05 19:00 UK on TikTok and YouTube (https://youtube.com/shorts/ee3fg-PsOds); see delivery/published.json.

ideas.title: The Vampire Case (Detective Max Sniffwell)
ideas.logline: Count Vlad, the nicest vampire in town, is knocked out cold with a slice of garlic bread by his coffin. The Chief offers Max a burger to drop it (red herring: he is just lazy). One long sniff: butter, fresh garlic, compost, so the garlic was homegrown, and only the gardener grows anything: a garlic patch behind the roses. Motive: Vlad kept the whole garden in the shade, twenty years of sad tomatoes. Cuffs on, gloves and all; with the garlic gone Vlad wakes, and his sister asks Max to stay for dinner. Then he sees the fangs. ~62 s.
ideas.notes: Script v1 'The Big Cheese' (Leo breaks out of jail, cheese-covered map, donut trap, sneeze cliffhanger) rejected 2026-10-05: the series is standalone cases. v2 is a clean take on the original's Vampire Case; v2 (94 s) cut to v3 (~62 s, new hook), then v4 (one clear clue chain; camping/respawn/floating dropped), then v5 (culprit is the gardener, not Leo again) the same day.

ideas.title: Whatever Mia Draws
ideas.logline: Anything Mia draws with her pencil comes to life exactly as drawn, and Mia can't draw: a stick dog, a square-wheeled bike, a stick boyfriend. Leo, the best artist in class, grabs the pencil and draws a perfect lion. Mia's wobbly cage holds but has no roof; her stick boyfriend gets batted like a toy, which shows her it's just a big cat. She scribbles a ball of yarn and the lion rolls over purring. For once, Mia drew something perfectly. Leo wants another go: 'No. You're too good.'
ideas.notes: Script v1 (196 words, ~78 s) too long; v2 cut to 153 words (~62-63 s, the new 61-65 s rule) 2026-10-05. Awaiting approval.

ideas.title: Catching the Egg Thief
ideas.logline: Steal an Egg base-defense heist: a hooded 50,000-speed thief robs Leo (900 speed) every night; laser door and capybara guard fail. Leo spends everything on one Mythic egg with a 60 s hatch timer and a Do Not Steal sign; it hatches in the thief's arms into a giant spinosaurus that knows its owner and carries the thief back by the hood. It's Max. He repays on the treadmill in four seconds and breaks it.

ideas.title: The Sandwich at My Door
ideas.logline: Every morning someone leaves Leo, who lives alone, a perfect sandwich and a caring note; on day 20 the note says 'Stop asking people. Just eat.' A hidden camera shows Leo himself sleepwalking at 3 a.m., making it and knocking on his own door. His thank-you note gets the reply 'We're out of bread.' Now he shops, his sleeping self cooks: best roommate ever.

ideas.title: The Guardian Quits
ideas.logline: Steal an Egg told by the guardian: a T-rex loses his egg at the safe-zone wall every day (BONK), gets a one-star review after 400 thefts, disguises himself as a 'Player' to cross the safe zone and steals every egg back from the bases (Leo bonks off him). All 400 hatch into baby T-rexes, so he quits to be Leo's base guard on a brainrot treadmill; his kids now bonk the wall.
ideas.notes: Scheduled 2026-10-09 19:00 UK on TikTok and YouTube; YouTube thumbnail is a stand-in frame, swap in the cover once channel verification clears.

ideas.title: Feeding the Prism Kitsune
ideas.logline: The Prism Kitsune falls out of the sky in Hunt For Eggs! and only eats Prism eggs. Leo learns five feeds make a Prism Chest; Max grinds the patrol and the Prism Alpha for the 5% Prism Blade and gets boosts; Mia takes the eggs and pulls the Blade from her first chest. Ends: 'Play Hunt for Eggs today. Link in bio!'
ideas.notes: Event ends 10:20 BST Fri 9 Oct 2026: post by Thu 8 Oct.

ideas.title: The Backwards Umbrella
ideas.logline: When Leo's umbrella is open it rains everywhere except under it. He soaks his friends, shares it (the Noob doesn't fit), keeps it shut - until Max's barbecue goes up in flames and the rain saves the park. Mia ducks under: 'Room for one more?'
ideas.notes: Park set, rain and fire effects; web route.

ideas.title: Anything Leo Pets
ideas.logline: Anything Leo pets with his gloves follows him forever: a puppy, kitten, goat and angry duck follow him to school and he can't lose them, so he stops petting things - until the zoo lion charges Max and Mia and he pets it. He throws the gloves away; Mia catches them, pats his head ('Good boy') and Leo becomes the pet.
ideas.notes: Animal parade (pack retriever, cat, goat, lion; duck stand-in); web route. Dropped 2026-10-05: user didn't like the concept.

ideas.title: Say Their Name
ideas.logline: In this obby, saying a player's name teleports them next to you; first to the top wins a million coins. Leo and Max keep summoning each other down, Leo's 'Steve' name tag fails, Mia summons both boys into mid-air over the lava - then tries the Noob, whose username takes so long to say he wins first, and her '...nine' teleports him to her holding a million coins.
ideas.notes: Approved 2026-10-05 ("approved, make the video"). Obby tower and lava, big name tags, teleport puffs; web route. Scheduled 2026-10-09 22:30 UK on TikTok. YouTube NOT uploaded yet (daily upload limit 2026-10-05): see delivery/published.json.

ideas.title: He Bought Google For 12 Dollars
ideas.logline: True story: in 2015 a former Google employee bought google.com for $12 on Google's own domain shop and owned it for a minute; Google cancelled it, paid a $6,006.13 bug reward (the digits spell GOOGLE) and doubled it when he gave it to a charity running free schools in India.
ideas.notes: Taken from OddFrame's top Short ('He Owned Google For A Minute', 32K views) at the user's request; own script and staging. Web route; laptop screen UI, digits-to-GOOGLE morph.

ideas.title: Detective Max Sniffwell: The Clown Case
ideas.logline: The mayoral candidate (a literal clown) has had his wife kidnapped on election day. One sniff of the ransom note: waffle cone, hot fudge, mint choc chip. At Big Scoop's Ice Cream Max finds her running the till: she faked it to buy an ice cream truck. He drags her back anyway; the clown wins; Max gets a black eye and a free sundae. Tempting.

ideas.title: Copy the Crown
ideas.logline: Every player copies whoever wears the crown; whoever has it when the timer ends wins a million coins. Leo walks Max off the edge into the lava, walks backwards so Max can never catch him, and makes the whole server dance. Mia flatters him into a bow, bows too, bonks the crown off his head and takes it; with three seconds left she steps back, and so do Leo and Max, who have been walking backwards all game: splash, splash.
ideas.notes: Approved 2026-10-05 ("approved, make the video"). Delivered for review 2026-10-05: delivery/Copy_the_Crown.mp4 (62.0 s incl. 0.5 s cover, -16.9 LUFS). Awaiting approval to post.

ideas.title: He Traded A Paperclip For A House
ideas.logline: True story: in 2005-06 a man traded one red paperclip up through 14 trades; his 'dumbest trade ever' (an afternoon with a rock star for a snow globe) got him a movie role from a snow-globe-collecting actor, and a tiny Canadian town traded him a two-storey house for the role.
ideas.notes: Approved 2026-10-05 ("approved, make the video"). Taken from OddFrame's 'He Traded a Paperclip for a House' (25K views). Narration 59.2 s (George voice C); web route, trade-window UI per swap, paperclip->house progress bar; encoded 61.7 s (incl. cover), awaiting approval.

ideas.title: He Ordered A Fighter Jet From Pepsi
ideas.logline: True story: in 1996 a student saw a Pepsi ad offer a fighter jet for 7,000,000 points, found extra points cost 10 cents, got five investors to front $700,000 and mailed the check; Pepsi sent it back with coupons, a judge ruled no reasonable person would believe the offer, and Pepsi re-ran the ad at 700,000,000 points with 'just kidding'.
ideas.notes: Taken from OddFrame's Pepsi Points fighter jet Short (26K views, one of their top Shorts) at the user's request ('make another story'); own script and staging. Web route; jet landing at a school as the hook, small-print zoom, number rolls, returned check and coupons, courtroom, 700,000,000 + JUST KIDDING payoff.

ideas.title: Lightning Hit Him Seven Times
ideas.logline: True story: a Shenandoah park ranger is hit by lightning seven times (1942-77) and survives them all; it finds him in a lookout tower, his truck, his yard, his office; he carries a water can for his hair, outruns a storm cloud only to be hit when he steps out, his boss walks off when lightning flashes, and on strike seven a bear steals his fish. The record still stands.
ideas.notes: Approved 2026-10-05 ("approved, make the video"). Delivered 2026-10-05 for review: delivery/Lightning_Hit_Him_Seven_Times.mp4 (64.4 s incl. 0.5 s cover, 1932 frames, -17.0 LUFS), cover, post.json/_post.md. Narration 62.1 s (George voice C, cloud). Web route, 28 shots, STRIKES 0/7 counter. New pack assets: ranger_hat (+ burnt museum copy), animal_bear_parts, brow-less faces. Picked through general research, not from OddFrame's list (Roy Sullivan, Guinness).

ideas.title: The Tornado Came Back
ideas.logline: True story: in March 1948 an unforecast tornado wrecks fifty planes at Tinker Air Force Base; the general asks why weathermen can forecast rain but not tornadoes. Five days later his two weathermen see the same weather map, call the odds billions to one, and still answer 'yes or no?' with yes. Planes go into hangars, one weatherman goes home wondering if he can get a job running an elevator, and at 6 pm a tornado hits almost the same spot: the first official tornado forecast comes true, and tornado warnings are born.
ideas.notes: Approved 2026-10-05 ("approved, make the video"). Narration 61.0 s (George voice C, cloud). User request 2026-10-05: 'Make a story about tornados'. Picked through general research, not from OddFrame's list (shortlist in source/story.md). Maj. Ernest Fawbush, Capt. Robert Miller, Maj. Gen. Fred Borum; named only in the post copy. Web route planned; tornado funnel, 1940s planes, hangars, radar scope, general's cap and elevator cap to build.

ideas.title: He Stole The Mona Lisa
ideas.logline: True story: in 1911 a former Louvre worker in a staff smock lifts the Mona Lisa off the wall, dumps the frame on a back staircase, and a plumber opens the locked door for him. Guards assume she's being photographed; police question Picasso; a detective leans on the table she's hidden in; crowds queue to stare at the empty wall. Two years later the Florence dealer he tries to sell her to calls the police. He stole a painting hardly anyone talked about and handed back the most famous painting in the world.
ideas.notes: Approved 2026-10-05 ("approved, make the video"). Narration 59.9 s (George voice C, cloud); video 61.9 s + 0.5 s cover. Web route, 22 shots; delivered for review: 62.4 s MP4 with cover, captions, post sheet. Picked through general research, not from OddFrame's list (Vincenzo Peruggia, 21 Aug 1911, recovered Dec 1913).

ideas.title: The Dog Who Found The World Cup
ideas.logline: True story: in March 1966 the World Cup is stolen from a guarded glass case in London, four months before England hosts the tournament. A ransom arrest catches only a middleman. A week later a collie called Pickles drags a newspaper parcel from under a hedge; his owner fears a bomb, tears it and reads 'Brazil, West Germany, Uruguay'. Police make the owner their main suspect; that summer England win and Pickles licks the players' plates at the victory dinner. Seventeen years later the trophy is stolen again in Brazil. This time there's no Pickles, and it's never been found.
ideas.notes: Approved 2026-10-05 ('Make it'). Narration 62.1 s (George voice C); video 64.5 s with end card and cover. Web route; new pack creature animal_collie_parts (retriever cut and recoloured). Full web render running. Pickles, David Corbett, theft 20 Mar 1966, found 27 Mar 1966, stolen again in Rio 19 Dec 1983.

ideas.title: He Mailed Himself Home
ideas.logline: True story: in 1964 an Australian athlete, broke in London, has his friend nail him into a crate labelled paint, sent cash on delivery to a company that doesn't exist. Fog in London, upside down on the tarmac in Bombay; 63 hours later he cuts his way out in Perth, walks out of the airport in his suit and hitchhikes home for his daughter's birthday. He forgets to tell his friend he survived; the friend calls a newspaper, the world finds out, and the airline drops the bill. He couldn't afford a ticket, and he never paid for one.
ideas.notes: Approved 2026-10-05 ("Make the video"). Narration 61.3 s (George voice C, cloud); video 63.4 s + 0.5 s cover. Web route, 24 shots; full web render running. Picked through general research, not from OddFrame's list (Reg Spiers, John McSorley, 17-20 Oct 1964; named only in the post copy).

ideas.title: He Flew A Lawn Chair
ideas.logline: True story: in 1982 a man who was never allowed to be a pilot ties 42 weather balloons to a lawn chair, meaning to float a hundred feet up on a rope. The rope snaps; he shoots to 16,000 feet, freezing, and two airline pilots radio the tower about a man in a lawn chair. He pops a few balloons with a pellet gun, drops the gun, drifts into power lines and blacks out a neighbourhood, lands unhurt, and the police are waiting. 'A man can't just sit around.' He's fined for flying an aircraft without calling the tower; the aircraft is a lawn chair, and today it sits in the Air and Space Museum.
ideas.notes: User request 2026-10-05: 'Make another story'. Picked through general research, not from OddFrame's list (Larry Walters, 'Inspiration I', San Pedro to Long Beach, 2 July 1982; named only in the post copy). Script v1 155 words with the CTA. Web route planned; thick glasses (new accessory), lawn chair with jugs, poppable balloon cluster, Jeep, power lines, airliner cockpit; reuse control tower, police car and museum. | Overnight run 2026-10-05/06 (no script approval needed): narration 59.8 s (George voice C, cloud), video 61.67 s + 0.5 s cover; web clip 20 shots; full web render done and encoded (62.2 s incl. cover, -16.4 LUFS, blank-frame check clean); delivered for the user's review, not posted.

ideas.title: He Flew The Wrong Way
ideas.logline: True story (1938): refused permission to fly the Atlantic, Douglas Corrigan files a flight plan to California, flies 28 hours east to Dublin, says "Just got in from New York. Where am I?" and blames his compass; his punishment ends the day his ship gets home, New York gives him a bigger parade than Lindbergh's, and he never admits a thing.
ideas.notes: Overnight run 2026-10-05: the user named this story and waived script approval for the run (write, then make the video; posting still needs approval). Script v1 156 words. Web route.

ideas.title: He Won The Marathon By Car
ideas.logline: True story: at the 1904 St. Louis Olympic marathon, in 90-degree heat and dust with one water stop, the first man across the line had ridden eleven miles in a car and nearly got the gold before officials heard about it; a Cuban mailman in cut-off street clothes chatted with the crowd, ate rotten orchard apples, napped, and still finished fourth; another runner was chased a mile off course by a dog.
ideas.notes: Overnight run 2026-10-05/06: story picked by the user; script approval waived for this run (posting still needs approval). Delivered for review: delivery/He_Won_The_Marathon_By_Car.mp4 (63.07 s). Narration 60.7 s (George voice C, gap 0.6 / beat 1.3). Web route. Fred Lorz, Andarin Carvajal, Len Taunyane named only in the post copy; strychnine/brandy only in the post description as history.

ideas.title: The Six Million Dollar Banana
ideas.logline: True story: a man pays $6.2 million for a banana, then eats it. It began in 2019 when an artist duct-taped a banana to a wall and sold it twice for $120,000; another artist ate it and the gallery just taped up a new one, because buyers get a certificate and instructions, not a banana. A student in Seoul ate one too. At auction in New York it went for $6.2 million and the buyer ate it on stage. The banana came from a street fruit stand: the man who sold it got 25 cents.
ideas.notes: Overnight batch (user 2026-10-05 23:45 UK: make as many story videos as possible, no script approval needed). Maurizio Cattelan, Comedian; David Datuna; Noh Hyun-soo; Justin Sun; Shah Alam: named only in the post copy. Script v1 159 words. Web route.

ideas.title: The Penguin General
ideas.logline: True story: a penguin inspects a line of soldiers, and they salute him because he outranks every one of them. In 1972 Norway's royal guard adopted a king penguin at Edinburgh Zoo, named him Nils Olav and made him a lance corporal; every visit since he gets promoted. The penguins change but the name and rank carry on. He was knighted with 130 soldiers on parade, got a bronze statue, became a brigadier and in 2023 a major general. Soldiers who trained for years salute him; he just waddles past.
ideas.notes: Overnight batch (user 2026-10-05 23:45 UK: make as many story videos as possible, no script approval needed). Sir Nils Olav III, Norwegian King's Guard, Edinburgh Zoo. Script v1 147 words. Web route; block penguin built in code.

ideas.title: He Won By Not Sleeping
ideas.logline: True story: 1983, Sydney to Melbourne, 544 miles. World-class runners line up, and so does a 61-year-old potato farmer in overalls. He shuffles; by nightfall he's miles behind. The pros sleep six hours; he wakes by mistake at 2 a.m., starts running, shuffles past their tents and leads by morning. He decides not to sleep at all, wins by ten hours, nearly two days under the record, and gives most of his $10,000 prize to the runners he beat.
ideas.notes: Overnight queue (user 2026-10-05: no script approval needed for these). Picked through general research (Cliff Young, 1983 Westfield Sydney-Melbourne ultramarathon; named only in the post copy). Script 162 words with the CTA. Web route.

ideas.title: They Lost A War To Emus
ideas.logline: True story: 1932, twenty thousand emus eat Western Australia's wheat. The army sends a major, two gunners, two machine guns and 10,000 bullets. The emus scatter, the gun jams at the ambush, the truck-mounted gun can't keep up or aim, every flock has a lookout. A week and 2,500 bullets later most emus are fine, Parliament jokes about medals, the army pulls out, and the major admits the birds face machine guns like tanks. The emus won.
ideas.notes: Overnight queue (no script approval needed). General research (Emu War, Nov 1932, Maj. G.P.W. Meredith; named only in the post copy). Picture rule: no emu is shown hit. Script 162 words with the CTA. Web route; code-built emus.

ideas.title: The Postman's Palace
ideas.logline: True story: in 1879 a French country postman trips over a strange stone, pockets it, and spends 33 years building a palace from stones he picks up on his 30 km round - pockets, then baskets, then a wheelbarrow, building at night by an oil lamp while the village laughs. 10,000 days later it's finished, with 'Let those who can do better, try' on the wall; refused burial inside it, he builds his own tomb in eight more years. Today it's a protected monument, and the village that laughed is famous because of him.
ideas.notes: Overnight run (user, 2026-10-05 23:45 UK: no script approval needed tonight). Ferdinand Cheval, Palais Ideal, Hauterives; named only in the post copy. Picked through general research. Web route; new postman_kepi accessory, procedural pebble palace that grows by clipping.

ideas.title: Spaghetti Grows On Trees
ideas.logline: True story (1 April 1957): Britain's most serious news show reports a bumper spaghetti harvest in Switzerland, pickers pulling spaghetti off trees, the weevil gone, every strand bred to the same length; eight million watch, hundreds phone in asking how to grow their own, and are told to put a sprig of spaghetti in a tin of tomato sauce and hope for the best. It was April Fools' Day.

ideas.title: She Went Over Niagara Falls In A Barrel
ideas.logline: True story: on her 63rd birthday in 1901, a broke schoolteacher who tells everyone she's twenty years younger climbs into a wooden barrel above Niagara Falls; her cat went over first as a test and survived; friends pump in air with a bicycle pump and set her adrift; she goes over the Horseshoe Falls and climbs out twenty minutes later with a cut on her head, alive ('never again'). Famous at last, she waits for the money, and her manager runs off with her barrel; she spends her savings on detectives to get it back.

ideas.title: She Raced Around The World
ideas.logline: True story: in 1889 a young reporter says she can beat the famous book's eighty days around the world; her editor wants to send a man. She sails two days later with one bag, meets the author, learns in Hong Kong that a rival was sent the other way the same day, loses two days to storms, races across America on a special train and finishes in 72 days, 6 hours, 11 minutes; the rival comes home four and a half days later.

ideas.title: The Dog Who Saved A Town
ideas.logline: True story: in 1925 a town in Alaska runs out of medicine with kids getting sick; ships can't get through the ice and planes can't fly in the cold, so twenty sled-dog teams relay it nearly seven hundred miles. One team gets the hardest part, led by a twelve-year-old dog called Togo: 170 miles just to reach it, then back across a frozen sea in a blizzard, and that night the storm blows the ice out to sea. 261 miles, more than any other team; the outbreak is stopped. But the statue in New York goes to the dog who ran the last 53 miles, Balto. Togo waits 76 years for his.

ideas.title: He Sold The Eiffel Tower
ideas.logline: True story: Paris, 1925. The papers say the Eiffel Tower is rusting and costly to fix, so con man Victor Lustig fakes government letters, invites scrap dealers to a fancy hotel and whispers that the tower is secretly being sold for scrap. Dealer Andre Poisson pays, and a bribe too; Lustig takes the train out of the country, and Poisson is too embarrassed to tell anyone, so Lustig comes back and tries it again. This time the police are called; he flees to America, tricks Al Capone, is caught making fake money, escapes down a rope and is caught again. His death certificate: apprentice salesman and counterfeiter.

ideas.title: The First Speeding Ticket
ideas.logline: True story: on 28 January 1896 in Kent, Walter Arnold becomes the first person charged with speeding, at 8 mph in a 2 mph zone; the law also wanted a crew of three with one walking ahead. A policeman chases him on a bicycle for five miles; he is charged with four offences at once. Months later the walker rule goes, the limit rises to 14 mph, and drivers celebrate with a run from London to Brighton that is still driven every year.

ideas.title: Miss Unsinkable
ideas.logline: True story: Violet Jessop works on ocean liners. Her ship the Olympic collides with a warship (nobody dies); the next year she's on its sister ship the Titanic, where an officer hands her a baby as she climbs into lifeboat 16 and she holds it until the rescue ship comes. Then she becomes a nurse on the third sister, the hospital ship Britannic, which hits a mine and sinks in under an hour; her lifeboat is pulled toward the propellers, she jumps, hits her head, and survives again. She works at sea for thirty more years: Miss Unsinkable.

ideas.title: He Declared Himself Emperor
ideas.logline: True story: in 1859 a broke San Francisco merchant, Joshua Norton, declares himself Emperor of the United States, and the city goes along with it. He lost his fortune trying to buy up all the rice in town; the newspaper prints his proclamation; he wears a uniform with gold epaulettes, prints his own money that shops accept, orders Congress shut down (ignored). Arrested once, the city is furious, the chief lets him go and officers salute him from then on. He orders a bridge across the bay; decades later it is built. Thousands line the streets for his funeral.
